correctness.rationale: Represent the random points by independent Dirichlet(1,1,1) barycentric coordinates. For squared sides p,q,r, D²=pB²+(p+q−r)BC+qC². Exact moments E[U1^i U2^j]=2i!j!/(i+j+2)! give M1=e1/18, M2=(e1²−2e2)/60, M3=23e1³/4200−31e1e2/2100+e3/210. Independently expanded the Dirichlet double sums symbolically for k=1,2,3, all polynomial differences identically zero. The nonzero e3 coefficient gives unique inversion and side polynomial, with strict triangle inequalities necessary and sufficient. Squared sides {1,4,4} and {2,2,5} share e1=9,e2=24 and area √15/4 yet have distinct e3, proving two moments insufficient. Forward sampling and exact population moments are expressly distinguished.
residual_risks: No finite-sample statistical stability or robustness theorem; all inverse statements require exact population moments.
The general symbolic proof relies on the correct Dirichlet barycentric distribution for independent area-uniform points, directly rederived.
